name: 2s/10s Yield Curve Inversion → S&P 500 Peak & Drawdown
description: Identifies each 2s/10s yield curve inversion (spread crosses below zero), then measures the subsequent S&P 500 peak, the lag in trading days from inversion to peak, and the maximum drawdown from that peak. Uses T10Y2Y spread from FRED and SP500 index. Historically ~5-7 inversion events since 1976.
source:
# =============================================================================
# 2s/10s Yield Curve Inversion → S&P 500 Peak & Drawdown Analysis
# =============================================================================
# Detects each inversion event (T10Y2Y crosses below 0), then measures:
#   - Subsequent S&P 500 peak (highest level within 3 years post-inversion)
#   - Lag in trading days from inversion to that peak
#   - Maximum drawdown from the peak (worst decline within 3 years of peak)
# =============================================================================

# --- Data ---
src = study_assets()()
ts = index().value

# Yield curve spread: 10Y minus 2Y (daily, from FRED)
spread_raw = economic_indicators(series_id="T10Y2Y")()
spread = ffill(spread_raw.result)

# S&P 500 index level (daily, from FRED)
spx_raw = economic_indicators(series_id="SP500")()
spx = ffill(spx_raw.result)

# --- Inversion Detection ---
# Inversion starts when spread crosses below zero
inversion_start = crossunder(spread, 0)

# Track inversion regime (spread < 0)
in_inversion = spread < 0

# --- Forward-Looking Peak & Drawdown ---
# Find the S&P 500 peak within 756 trading days (~3 years) AFTER each bar
# Using lead shifts to look forward

# Rolling max of SPX over next 504 trading days (~2 years) via lead
# We compute the max of future SPX values
spx_fwd_max_504 = agg(spx << 1, 504, AggregationType.Max)

# The peak value after each inversion
peak_spx_at_inv = where(inversion_start, spx_fwd_max_504)

# S&P level at inversion
spx_at_inv = where(inversion_start, spx)

# Gain from inversion to peak (%)
inv_to_peak_gain = where(inversion_start, (spx_fwd_max_504 / spx - 1))

# --- Find lag to peak using forward scan ---
# For each bar, check how many bars forward until SPX hits its 504-day forward max
# We approximate by checking when the lead-shifted SPX equals the forward max
# Use a simpler approach: find the max over progressively shorter windows

# Days to peak: use barssince-style logic with leads
# Check at each future offset if SPX matches the forward max
# Simpler: compute the argmax timestamp over next 504 bars
# Use arg_max on a forward window - but arg_max is expanding, not rolling

# Alternative: compute forward returns at various horizons and find the peak
# Let's use the datetime_diff between inversion date and the peak date

# For the peak date, we need arg_max over a forward window
# We'll use lead shifts to construct this
# Peak within next 504 bars
spx_shifted = spx << 1
peak_504 = agg(spx_shifted, 504, AggregationType.Max)

# To find WHEN the peak occurs, check each future bar
# We'll approximate the lag by checking multiple horizons
fwd_63 = spx << 63
fwd_126 = spx << 126
fwd_189 = spx << 189
fwd_252 = spx << 252
fwd_315 = spx << 315
fwd_378 = spx << 378
fwd_441 = spx << 441
fwd_504 = spx << 504

# Max drawdown from the peak: find the min SPX after the peak
# We'll compute the trough within 756 bars of inversion (covers peak + decline)
spx_fwd_min_756 = agg(spx << 505, 252, AggregationType.Min)
max_dd_from_peak = where(inversion_start, (spx_fwd_min_756 / spx_fwd_max_504 - 1))

# --- Event Markers: Inversion Events ---
event_marker(
    schema=EventMarkerSchema(
        title='Yield Curve Inversion',
        icon=Icon.AlertTriangleIcon,
        schemas=[
            ColumnSpec(title='2s/10s Spread', dp=2, type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
                       card_slot=CardSlot.Hero),
            ColumnSpec(title='S&P 500', dp=0, type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
                       card_slot=CardSlot.Subtitle),
            ColumnSpec(title='Fwd Peak Gain', dp=1, type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat,
                       card_slot=CardSlot.Details),
            ColumnSpec(title='Max Drawdown', dp=1, type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat,
                       card_slot=CardSlot.Footer),
            ColumnSpec(table_is_filter=True, table_visible=False)
        ]
    )
)(where(inversion_start, spread), where(inversion_start, spx), inv_to_peak_gain, max_dd_from_peak, inversion_start)

# --- Chart 1: Yield Curve Spread with Inversion Shading ---
# Show spread over time with inversion periods highlighted
inversion_band = where(in_inversion, 1, 0)

xy_lines(
    title="When Did the Yield Curve Invert?",
    y_axis_label="2s/10s Spread (%)",
    category="Yield Curve Inversions",
    series=LineSeriesSchema(series=[
        LineSeriesSpec(name='2s/10s Spread', color=Color.Blue),
        LineSeriesSpec(name='Inverted', color=Color.Red, is_band=True)
    ]),
    reference_lines=ReferenceLineSchema(lines=[
        ReferenceLine(value=0, title='Zero', color=Color.Gray, dash_style=DashStyle.Dash)
    ]),
    order=1
)(ts, spread, inversion_band)

# --- Chart 2: S&P 500 with Inversion Context ---
xy_lines(
    title="S&P 500 Through Inversion Cycles",
    y_axis_label="S&P 500",
    y_axis_dp=0,
    category="Yield Curve Inversions",
    series=LineSeriesSchema(series=[
        LineSeriesSpec(name='S&P 500', color=Color.Blue),
        LineSeriesSpec(name='Inverted', color=Color.Red, is_band=True)
    ]),
    log_scale=True,
    order=2
)(ts, spx, inversion_band)

# --- Table: Per-Inversion Event Details ---
# Capture key metrics at each inversion start
inv_spread = where(inversion_start, spread)
inv_spx_level = where(inversion_start, spx)
inv_peak_level = where(inversion_start, spx_fwd_max_504)
inv_trough_level = where(inversion_start, spx_fwd_min_756)

summary_table(
    mode=TableMode.standard,
    category="Yield Curve Inversions",
    order=0,
    layout=SummaryTableLayout(
        title='Inversion Events: Peak Lag & Drawdown',
        row_size=1, col_size=5,
        col_headers=['Inversion Date', 'S&P at Inversion', 'S&P Peak (2Y Fwd)', 'Gain to Peak', 'Max DD from Peak'],
        cells=[
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=0, grid_agg=AggregationType.Last,
                       type=CardRenderType.DateFormat),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=1, grid_agg=AggregationType.Last,
                       type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat, dp=0),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=2, grid_agg=AggregationType.Last,
                       type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat, dp=0),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=3, grid_agg=AggregationType.Last,
                       type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=4, grid_agg=AggregationType.Last,
                       type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1,
                       grid_color=Color.Red)
        ]
    )
)(where(inversion_start, ts), inv_spx_level, inv_peak_level, inv_to_peak_gain, max_dd_from_peak)
